title: A color can be saved as a named style and reused
goal: Components should share their colors rather than each carrying its own. Saving a fill as a named style lets any layer point at it, and editing the style repaints everything pointing at it in one step.
notes:
Step D8 of docs/design/ui-building.md. Tokens (where a name resolves differently per light and dark mode) are deliberately deferred; styles gain token backing when modes arrive. From dsys.html and ds-build-wt.html: save as style, then components bind to the name.

Sequenced BEFORE the built-in components by the 2026-09-03 retriage, which is the reverse of steps 7 and 8 in docs/design/ui-building.md. The doc puts the starter set at 7 and styles at 8, but step 7 requires the starter components to be drawn from named styles rather than raw colors, which cannot happen until styles exist. Swapping them is the smaller change; the alternative is to let the starter set ship with raw colors and re-do it, which is worse. The built-in components task now depends on this one.

Objective: ui-components (staged now, under the focus). Named styles are the later ui-design-systems epic in miniature, and only this much of it is in scope: the starter components are specified as built from styles, so styles have to exist first.
acceptance: A selected fill can be saved as a named style, and it appears in the Library styles section
A layer can be set to use a style instead of a raw color, and the inspector says which style it is using
Editing a style repaints every layer using it in one undo step
A layer using no style behaves exactly as today
Core logic is covered by tests in PhotonzCore written before the implementation
Audit written under queue/audits/, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Adversarial review, before building. (1) The mock (ds-build-wt) hangs Save as style off a Fill section that does not exist here: in the app a shape's fill lives in the Annotation section, a frame's surface in the Frame section, text ink in the Text section. Building the mock's Fill section would duplicate controls, so the affordance attaches to the rows that already exist. (2) The mock shows a style already named (Brand / gradient) and no naming step. A first timer needs to name it, and a modal for one word is heavy, so saving reuses the flow Make Component already taught: the style is made with a placeholder name, the Library flips to Styles, the new tile is picked and its name field takes focus with the text selected. (3) The mock's example style is a gradient. Photonz fills are solid hexes, so this builds solid color styles only. (4) Applying a style from the Library is impossible without breaking the one selection model: picking a tile clears the layer selection by design. So binding happens in the inspector, where the layer is still selected, and the Library is where a style is renamed, recolored and deleted. (5) Editing a bound color by hand: rather than silently repainting the person's edit back to the style, a bound row shows the style name instead of the color well, so the only way to a raw color is Unlink, said out loud. A safety net in the model unlinks any bound color some other path (paint bucket, paste) changes, so the row can never claim a style it is not wearing. (6) Shortest version that delivers the value: solid color styles on three slots (a shape's fill, a shape's ink, text ink) plus a frame's surface, which is what a starter button, card or badge is painted from.

Built and verified. Core: Sources/PhotonzCore/ColorStyles.swift (ColorStyle, ColorSlot, ColorStyleBinding, save/bind/unlink/recolor/rename/delete, colorStyleLibraryEntries, reconcileColorStyles) plus stored colorStyles on the document and colorStyleBindings on the layer, both written only when non-empty so old documents encode unchanged. 30 tests in ColorStyleTests written before the implementation; suite green at 1826. App: Sources/Photonz/ColorStylePanel.swift (the styles menu on a color row, the name field saving opens, the Styles shelf tile, the picked style's section), wired into the Annotation Fill and Color rows, the Text Color row and the Frame Background row, behind next-styles (needs next-library). Verified end to end on the probe with Scripts/playtest/styles-walk.json: draw a box, Save as Style, type Accent, draw a second box, use the style, recolor it on the shelf, both repaint, one undo puts both back. Real screen captures in queue/audits/.

Adversarial review of the built thing, on the real app. Two things were wrong and are fixed: the styled row printed the style's name with no color at all (a swatch inside a menu label is dropped by AppKit, so the row draws the color next door now), and the name field had nowhere to live because saving keeps the LAYER selected, not the new tile (so naming moved into a field under the color row, which also made it drivable by a walk). One thing stands, in the audit's rough: a style can only be applied to one layer at a time, and nothing says out loud when a color lets go of its style. Both are filed.

Named color styles ship in Next behind next-styles. Core in Sources/PhotonzCore/ColorStyles.swift with 30 tests written first (suite green, 1826); UI in Sources/Photonz/ColorStylePanel.swift on the Fill, Color and Background rows plus the Library's Styles shelf. Verified end to end on the probe app with Scripts/playtest/styles-walk.json and real screen captures; audit at queue/audits/2026-09-03-color-styles.json. Two follow-ups filed.
